NBA Prediction Model

Win probability, score and total come from the game model (regularized logistic and ridge regressions trained on every earlier game; see notebooks 1–3). Open a game for its box score: each player's average projected line, with minutes adding up to 240 and points to the predicted score, or simulate one realistic game.

▲ above / ▼ below his typical game · shaded = 15%+

Rank among 30 teams in what each defense allows to each position (1st = allows the least). Green = one of the 6 softest matchups, orange = one of the 6 toughest. Small number = allowed per game. This season and last season blended by games played.

Shot diet allowed

What kind of shots each defense gives up, compared with what the same opponents normally take (their previous 40 games, last season included). Green = gives up more, orange = fewer. A shot funnel shows up as more threes and fewer twos; some defenses leave below-average shooters open in particular. The model moves each player's threes, twos, free throws and points by these according to his own shot mix ().

How the model learns

Every day's run adds the previous night's box scores and retrains a machine-learning model on every logged game. It learns from recent form, minutes, rest and back-to-backs, home/away, both teams' pace, what the opponent has allowed to the position lately, and missing teammates, and is blended with the formula model ().
